question: As of April 2025, what amount of monthly pension is given to players under Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons (PDUNWFS) scheme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹5,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons (PDUNWFS)** was established in **1982** with the aim to assist outstanding sportspersons who have brought glory to the nation in sports but are now facing financial distress.
 
• As per the scheme, eligible players receive a **monthly pension of ₹5,000** under the **Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons (PDUNWFS)**.
 
• It aims to provide **financial stability** to sportspersons who have contributed significantly to Indian sports but are now in need of assistance due to old age or other circumstances.
 
• This scheme is part of the government’s broader efforts to **honor and support sportspersons** for their valuable contributions to national pride and development in sports.
 
• The pension amount of **₹5,000** is provided to ensure a decent living standard for retired or financially distressed athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About PDUNWFS:**

 
 
• The **Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Fund for Sportspersons** was set up by the Government of India under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• The scheme addresses the financial needs of sportspersons who are facing hardships due to their inability to earn a livelihood after retirement from active sports.
 
• It also provides **one-time financial assistance** to sportspersons or their families for medical treatment, education, and other needs.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The scheme primarily benefits **former sportspersons** who have represented India at international levels, such as the Olympics, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, and other recognized championships.
 
• To qualify for the monthly pension, sportspersons must have retired from active sports and should not be earning sufficient income for a stable livelihood.
 
 
 
• **Government Support:**
 
 
• The Indian government has consistently worked to **promote sports and welfare schemes** for athletes to ensure they receive adequate support post-retirement.
 
• Other schemes for sportspersons include **National Sports Development Fund (NSDF)** and the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Government Schemes:**
 
 
• Similar to PDUNWFS, the **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** also provides monthly pension benefits for individuals in the unorganized sector.
 
• However, PDUNWFS is specifically tailored for retired or financially distressed sportspersons, focusing on their contribution to sports.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PDUNWFS:**
 
 
• The scheme has supported several athletes in distress, helping them lead a dignified life after their active sports career.
 
• It serves as a recognition of their invaluable contribution to **India’s sports legacy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **monthly pension amount of ₹5,000** under PDUNWFS is a fixed benefit provided to eligible sportspersons.
 
• The fund can also provide **one-time financial assistance** for medical emergencies or other essential needs of the sportspersons or their families.
 
• This scheme is a significant initiative under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to **ensure social security** for athletes who have represented India at prestigious platforms.
 
• Sportspersons or their families can apply for benefits under this scheme through the respective sports federations or the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• It reflects the government’s commitment to **encouraging sports culture** in India while ensuring the well-being of retired athletes.
